## Description

The `firmwareUpdateProgress` event is published on the management event channel while an OS update is running.

The reader publishes progress events until the update completes or fails.

This event includes:

- The current update status.
- Image download progress.
- Overall update progress.
- Per-component update progress for OS, root file system, applications, radio firmware, and platform.

This event is useful when the backend must track the progress of an OS update after the update is started.

## Event details

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| MQTT event | `firmwareUpdateProgress` |
| Envelope `type` | `firmwareUpdateProgress` |
| Configuration path | Not configurable in `managementEventConfig` |
| Trigger | `set_os` |
| Delivery destination | `endpointConfig.management.event` |
| Communication type | Device to Cloud |
| Applies to | FXR readers |

## How firmware progress works

This event does not have a `managementEventConfig` enable or disable flag.

Set the destination in [Configure Management Events](#tag-management-events-configure-management-events). After the destination is configured, start the OS update by using `set_os`.

When the update starts, the reader automatically publishes `firmwareUpdateProgress` events on the management-event destination until the update completes or fails.

## Fields

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `status` | Current update status. Values include `started`, `failed`, `rebooting`, `downloading-<image>`, `erasing-<image>`, and `writing-<image>`. |
| `imageDownloadProgress` | Image download progress, from `0` to `100`. |
| `overallUpdateProgress` | Overall update progress, from `0` to `100`. |
| `updateProgressDetails` | Per-component update progress. This includes `os`, `rootFileSystem`, `applications`, `radioFirmware`, and `platform`. If the update fails, this field can contain a failure reason string. |

## Firmware update progress event schema

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | Always `firmwareUpdateProgress`. |
| `timestamp` | string | Event timestamp. |
| `component` | string | Component that published the event. |
| `eventNum` | number | Management event sequence number. |
| `data.status` | string | Current firmware update status. |
| `data.imageDownloadProgress` | number | Image download progress percentage. |
| `data.overallUpdateProgress` | number | Overall update progress percentage. |
| `data.updateProgressDetails` | object or string | Per-component update progress, or a failure reason string when the update fails. |

type.description: Management event type.

timestamp.description: Event timestamp with UTC offset. Reader examples may use +0000 instead of +00:00.

component.description: Event source: RG for Reader Gateway, RC for Radio Control, or the user application name.

status.description: Update status, such as started, failed, rebooting, downloading-<image>, erasing-<image>, or writing-<image>; <image> is the image name.

rootFileSystem.description: root file system update progress percentage

## GPI Events

The reader publishes a `gpi` event on the management event channel when a GPI pin changes between `HIGH` and `LOW`.

### Configure GPI events

Complete the following three steps in order.

#### Step 1: Configure the management-event destination

Configure the management-event destination as described in [Configure Management Event Publishing](#tag-management-events-configure-management-event-publishing).

#### Step 2: Configure event publication

Enable or disable GPI event publication under:

```text
READER-GATEWAY.managementEventConfig.gpiEvents
```

| Configuration field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpiEvents` | boolean | Set to `true` to publish GPI events or `false` to disable publication. |

#### Step 3: Apply the configuration

Apply the configuration using [`set_config`](set_config.md) for MQTT or `PUT /cloud/config` for REST. Select the corresponding example below to view the complete request.

### Published GPI event

A GPI event uses the common management-event envelope with `type` set to `gpi`.

The event-specific `data` object contains the following fields:

| Event field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data.pin` | integer | GPI pin that changed: `1`, `2`, `3`, or `4`. |
| `data.state` | string | New state of the pin: `HIGH` or `LOW`. |

#### GPI event body

Use the **Sample GPI Event** tab to view an event published by the reader. Use the **GPI Event Schema** tab to review the complete event structure.

type.description: Management event type.

timestamp.description: Event timestamp with UTC offset. Reader examples may use +0000 instead of +00:00.

component.description: Event source: RG for Reader Gateway, RC for Radio Control, or the user application name.

pin.description: GPI pin number. FXR readers have 4 GPI pins (1–4).

command.description: Command name.

command_id.description: Caller-supplied request identifier.

payload.description: Reader configuration update.

## Error Events

Error events notify applications when the reader detects a configured error condition. The reader publishes these events on the management event channel.

### Configure error events

Complete the following three steps in order.

#### Step 1: Configure the management-event destination

Configure the management-event destination as described in [Configure Management Event Publishing](#tag-management-events-configure-management-event-publishing).

#### Step 2: Configure error reporting

Configure error reporting under:

```text
READER-GATEWAY.managementEventConfig.errors
```

The `errors` object determines which error conditions the reader reports. Set a supported Boolean field to `true` to enable error reporting for that condition or `false` to disable it.

##### Supported error monitors

| Field under `errors` | Type    | Description                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `antenna`            | boolean | Enables or disables antenna connection error reporting.                                            |
| `database`           | boolean | Enables or disables database error reporting.                                                      |
| `ntp`                | boolean | Enables or disables NTP synchronization error reporting.                                           |
| `radio`              | boolean | Enables or disables radio error reporting.                                                         |
| `radio_control`      | boolean | Enables or disables Radio Control error reporting.                                                 |
| `reader_gateway`     | boolean | Enables or disables Reader Gateway error reporting.                                                |
| `cpu`                | object  | Configures CPU-utilization error reporting.                                                        |
| `ram`                | object  | Configures RAM-utilization error reporting.                                                        |
| `flash`              | object  | Configures flash-utilization error reporting.                                                      |
| `userApp`            | object  | Configures reporting when a user application does not send a heartbeat within the configured time. |

##### Resource monitor settings

The `cpu`, `ram`, and `flash` objects support the following fields:

| Field                 | Type   | Description                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `threshold`           | number | Utilization percentage that triggers an error event. Supported values are `1` through `99`. The default is `90`. |
| `reportIntervalInSec` | number | Minimum interval, in seconds, between repeated reports for the same condition. The default is `1800`.            |

##### User application monitor settings

| Field                 | Type   | Description                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `threshold`           | number | Time, in seconds, that the reader waits without receiving an application heartbeat before reporting an error. |
| `reportIntervalInSec` | number | Interval, in seconds, between repeated reports for the same condition.                                        |

## Warning Events

Warning events notify applications when the reader detects a condition that requires attention. The reader publishes these events on the management event channel.

### Configure warning events

Complete the following three steps in order.

#### Step 1: Configure the management-event destination

Configure the management-event destination as described in [Configure Management Event Publishing](#tag-management-events-configure-management-event-publishing).

#### Step 2: Configure warning reporting

Configure warning reporting under:

```text
READER-GATEWAY.managementEventConfig.warnings
```

The `warnings` object determines which warning conditions the reader reports.

##### Supported warning monitors

| Field under `warnings` | Type              | Description                                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cpu`                  | object            | Configures CPU-utilization warning reporting.                                    |
| `ram`                  | object            | Configures RAM-utilization warning reporting.                                    |
| `flash`                | object            | Configures flash-utilization warning reporting.                                  |
| `temperature`          | object            | Configures ambient and power-amplifier temperature warning thresholds.           |
| `ntp`                  | boolean or object | Enables NTP synchronization warnings or configures NTP-offset warning reporting. |
| `database`             | boolean           | Enables or disables database warning reporting.                                  |
| `radio_api`            | boolean           | Enables or disables Radio API warning reporting.                                 |
| `radio_control`        | boolean           | Enables or disables Radio Control warning reporting.                             |
| `reader_gateway`       | boolean           | Enables or disables Reader Gateway warning reporting.                            |
| `userApp`              | object            | Configures user-application resource-usage warning reporting.                    |

Set a Boolean field to `true` to enable the corresponding warning reports or `false` to disable them.

##### Resource monitor settings

The `cpu`, `ram`, `flash`, and `userApp` objects support the following fields:

| Field                 | Type   | Description                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `threshold`           | number | Utilization percentage above which the reader publishes a warning event.               |
| `reportIntervalInSec` | number | Minimum interval, in seconds, between repeated reports for the same warning condition. |

The supported utilization threshold is `1` through `99`.

The default threshold is:

* `80` for `cpu`
* `80` for `flash`
* `90` for `ram`

The default `reportIntervalInSec` is `1800`.

##### Temperature monitor settings

The `temperature` object supports the following fields:

| Field     | Type   | Description                                                                      |
| --------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ambient` | number | Ambient-temperature threshold, in degrees Celsius. The default is `75`.          |
| `pa`      | number | Power-amplifier temperature threshold, in degrees Celsius. The default is `105`. |

The reader publishes a warning event when either configured temperature threshold is exceeded.

##### NTP monitor settings

Set `ntp` to a Boolean value to enable or disable NTP synchronization warning reporting:

```json
"ntp": true
```

## Tag Data Events

Tag Data Events report RFID tag reads on the configured data event channel while inventory is active.

The event’s `type` value identifies the operating mode that produced the tag read:

* `SIMPLE` — Reads and reports every unique tag with the basic identity fields. For details, see [SIMPLE Tag Data Events](#op-simple_tag_data_events).
* `INVENTORY` — Reports unique tags for each antenna at a configured interval, including peak RSSI and read count. For details, see [INVENTORY Tag Data Events](#op-inventory_tag_data_events).
* `CUSTOM` — Supports an advanced inventory workflow with optional metadata and tag-access results. For details, see [CUSTOM Tag Data Events](#op-custom_tag_data_events).
* `PORTAL` — Reports unique tags after a GPI trigger starts the portal read cycle. For details, see [PORTAL Tag Data Events](#op-portal_tag_data_events).
* `CONVEYOR` — Reports unique tags for each antenna using the conveyor workflow. For details, see [CONVEYOR Tag Data Events](#op-conveyor_tag_data_events).

These values represent operating modes, not separate event categories. All modes use the same Tag Data Event envelope, but the fields published inside `data` depend on the active mode and its configuration.

### Configure tag data event publishing

Complete the following four steps before receiving tag data events.

#### Step 1: Configure the data-event destination

Use [`set_importCloudConfig`](set_importCloudConfig.md) to configure the connection and publish topic under:

```text
endpointConfig.data.event
```

Select the **MQTT tag data events** example on the `set_importCloudConfig` page to view the complete configuration.

#### Step 2: Configure the operating mode

Use [`set_mode`](set_mode.md) to select and configure the required operating mode.

The operating mode determines the default fields included in each Tag Data Event.

| Operating mode | Default fields in `data`                                      | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`SIMPLE`](#op-simple_tag_data_events)       | `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                                 | Publishes the basic RFID tag-read fields.                                                                                                    |
| [`INVENTORY`](#op-inventory_tag_data_events)    | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`, `peakRssi`, `reads` | Publishes tag identity, antenna, signal-strength, and read-count information.                                                                |
| [`CUSTOM`](#op-custom_tag_data_events)       | `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                                 | Publishes tag reads using the configured custom inventory workflow. Optional metadata and access-operation results may add fields to `data`. |
| [`PORTAL`](#op-portal_tag_data_events)       | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                      | Publishes tag reads after the configured portal trigger starts the read cycle.                                                               |
| [`CONVEYOR`](#op-conveyor_tag_data_events)     | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                      | Publishes tag reads using the configured conveyor workflow.                                                                                  |

#### Step 3: Select optional tag metadata

Use `tagMetaData` in the `set_mode` configuration to select additional information to include with each tag read.

`tagMetaData` is a configuration property. It is not included as a field in the published event. Each selected metadata value adds its corresponding field directly to the event’s `data` object.

For example, this configuration:

```json
"tagMetaData": [
  "ANTENNA",
  "RSSI",
  "SEEN_COUNT"
]
```

adds the following fields to the published event:

```json
"data": {
  "antenna": 1,
  "peakRssi": -37,
  "reads": 1
}
```

The following table shows the verified metadata-to-event-field mappings:

| `tagMetaData` selection | Published field in `data` |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `ANTENNA`               | `antenna`                 |
| `RSSI`                  | `peakRssi`                |
| `SEEN_COUNT`            | `reads`                   |
| `CHANNEL`               | `channel`                 |
| `PHASE`                 | `phase`                   |
| `PC`                    | `PC`                      |
| `XPC`                   | `XPC`                     |
| `CRC`                   | `CRC`                     |
| `TID`                   | `TID`                     |
| `USER`                  | `USER`                    |
| `userDefined` object    | `userDefined`             |
| `antennaNames` object   | `antennaPortNames`        |

Not every metadata selection is supported in every operating mode. See [`set_mode`](set_mode.md) for the supported mode configuration and field restrictions.

#### Step 4: Start inventory

Use [`start`](start.md) to start inventory.

After inventory starts, the reader publishes Tag Data Events automatically to the topic configured under `endpointConfig.data.event`.

### Published tag data event

A Tag Data Event contains the following outer fields:

| Field       | Type   | Description                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`      | string | Operating mode that produced the tag read.                                                |
| `timestamp` | string | Date and time when the reader generated the event, including its UTC offset.              |
| `data`      | object | Tag-read information. The included fields depend on the operating mode and configuration. |

The `data` object always contains `eventNum`, `format`, and `idHex`. Other fields are included according to the operating mode, selected tag metadata, report filtering, and configured tag access operations.

Use the **Sample Tag Data Event** tab to compare examples for `SIMPLE`, `INVENTORY`, `CUSTOM`, `PORTAL`, and `CONVEYOR` modes. Use the **Tag Data Event Schema** tab to review all possible event fields. The operating-mode table above identifies the fields published by default in each mode.

type.description: RFID operating mode that produced the event.

## Tag Data Events

Tag Data Events report RFID tag reads on the configured data event channel while inventory is active.

The event’s `type` value identifies the operating mode that produced the tag read:

* `SIMPLE` — Reads and reports every unique tag with the basic identity fields. For details, see [SIMPLE Tag Data Events](#op-simple_tag_data_events).
* `INVENTORY` — Reports unique tags for each antenna at a configured interval, including peak RSSI and read count. For details, see [INVENTORY Tag Data Events](#op-inventory_tag_data_events).
* `CUSTOM` — Supports an advanced inventory workflow with optional metadata and tag-access results. For details, see [CUSTOM Tag Data Events](#op-custom_tag_data_events).
* `PORTAL` — Reports unique tags after a GPI trigger starts the portal read cycle. For details, see [PORTAL Tag Data Events](#op-portal_tag_data_events).
* `CONVEYOR` — Reports unique tags for each antenna using the conveyor workflow. For details, see [CONVEYOR Tag Data Events](#op-conveyor_tag_data_events).

These values represent operating modes, not separate event categories. All modes use the same Tag Data Event envelope, but the fields published inside `data` depend on the active mode and its configuration.

### Configure tag data event publishing

Complete the following four steps before receiving tag data events.

#### Step 1: Configure the data-event destination

Use [`set_importCloudConfig`](set_importCloudConfig.md) to configure the connection and publish topic under:

```text
endpointConfig.data.event
```

Select the **MQTT tag data events** example on the `set_importCloudConfig` page to view the complete configuration.

#### Step 2: Configure the operating mode

Use [`set_mode`](set_mode.md) to select and configure the required operating mode.

The operating mode determines the default fields included in each Tag Data Event.

| Operating mode | Default fields in `data`                                      | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`SIMPLE`](#op-simple_tag_data_events)       | `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                                 | Publishes the basic RFID tag-read fields.                                                                                                    |
| [`INVENTORY`](#op-inventory_tag_data_events)    | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`, `peakRssi`, `reads` | Publishes tag identity, antenna, signal-strength, and read-count information.                                                                |
| [`CUSTOM`](#op-custom_tag_data_events)       | `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                                 | Publishes tag reads using the configured custom inventory workflow. Optional metadata and access-operation results may add fields to `data`. |
| [`PORTAL`](#op-portal_tag_data_events)       | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                      | Publishes tag reads after the configured portal trigger starts the read cycle.                                                               |
| [`CONVEYOR`](#op-conveyor_tag_data_events)     | `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, `idHex`                      | Publishes tag reads using the configured conveyor workflow.                                                                                  |

#### Step 3: Select optional tag metadata

Use `tagMetaData` in the `set_mode` configuration to select additional information to include with each tag read.

`tagMetaData` is a configuration property. It is not included as a field in the published event. Each selected metadata value adds its corresponding field directly to the event’s `data` object.

For example, this configuration:

```json
"tagMetaData": [
  "ANTENNA",
  "RSSI",
  "SEEN_COUNT"
]
```

adds the following fields to the published event:

```json
"data": {
  "antenna": 1,
  "peakRssi": -37,
  "reads": 1
}
```

The following table shows the verified metadata-to-event-field mappings:

| `tagMetaData` selection | Published field in `data` |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `ANTENNA`               | `antenna`                 |
| `RSSI`                  | `peakRssi`                |
| `SEEN_COUNT`            | `reads`                   |
| `CHANNEL`               | `channel`                 |
| `PHASE`                 | `phase`                   |
| `PC`                    | `PC`                      |
| `XPC`                   | `XPC`                     |
| `CRC`                   | `CRC`                     |
| `TID`                   | `TID`                     |
| `USER`                  | `USER`                    |
| `userDefined` object    | `userDefined`             |
| `antennaNames` object   | `antennaPortNames`        |

Not every metadata selection is supported in every operating mode. See [`set_mode`](set_mode.md) for the supported mode configuration and field restrictions.

#### Step 4: Start inventory

Use [`start`](start.md) to start inventory.

After inventory starts, the reader publishes Tag Data Events automatically to the topic configured under `endpointConfig.data.event`.

### Published tag data event

A Tag Data Event contains the following outer fields:

| Field       | Type   | Description                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`      | string | Operating mode that produced the tag read.                                                |
| `timestamp` | string | Date and time when the reader generated the event, including its UTC offset.              |
| `data`      | object | Tag-read information. The included fields depend on the operating mode and configuration. |

The `data` object always contains `eventNum`, `format`, and `idHex`. Other fields are included according to the operating mode, selected tag metadata, report filtering, and configured tag access operations.

Use the **Sample Tag Data Event** tab to compare examples for `SIMPLE`, `INVENTORY`, `CUSTOM`, `PORTAL`, and `CONVEYOR` modes. Use the **Tag Data Event Schema** tab to review all possible event fields. The operating-mode table above identifies the fields published by default in each mode.

SIMPLE mode configures the radio to read and report all unique tags in the field of view of the radio.

Tag reads published during PORTAL mode use the common RFID envelope with `type: "PORTAL"`.

The default `data` fields are `antenna`, `eventNum`, `format`, and `idHex`. Events are published after the configured GPI trigger starts the read cycle. Additional fields depend on supported metadata selections.

## Mode Behavior

PORTAL mode configures the radio to report all unique tags that pass by each antenna immediately following a GPI event. The GPI event signals the beginning of the read period. As soon as the GPI event triggers the radio, the radio continues to read tags until no new unique tags are read for a configurable stop interval. Once the radio stops reading tags, it waits for the next GPI event to start the process again.

**Default behavior:**

* The radio attempts to read tags on all antennas. This can be adjusted using the `antennas` object when setting the mode.
* The radio reports all unique tags once. This can be adjusted using the `filter` object when setting the mode.
* The radio waits for a LOW signal on GPI 1. This can be adjusted using the `startTrigger` object when setting the mode.
* The radio continues to read until no new unique tags have been read for 3 seconds. This can be adjusted using the `stopInterval` object when setting the mode.

See [Tag Data Events](tagDataEvents.md) for the envelope and [Set Mode](set_mode.md) for supported configuration.

## BLE Data Events

BLE Data Events report Bluetooth Low Energy devices and beacon advertisements detected by the reader. The reader publishes these events on the configured data event channel while BLE scanning is running.

BLE Data Events use `BLE_DATA` as the event `type`.

### Configure BLE data event publishing

Complete the following three steps before receiving BLE data events.

#### Step 1: Verify the data-event connection

BLE Data Events use the same data-event connection as RFID Tag Data Events. There is no separate destination configuration for BLE events.

If a data-event connection has not already been configured, use [`set_importCloudConfig`](set_importCloudConfig.md) to add a connection under:

```text
endpointConfig.data.event
```

See [`set_importCloudConfig`](set_importCloudConfig.md) for the supported connection types and configuration examples.

#### Step 2: Configure BLE scanning

Use [`set_bleConfig`](set_bleConfig.md) to configure BLE scanning.

Set:

```text
payload.ble.enable
```

to `true`.

The BLE configuration also determines:

* The scan interval
* The enabled BLE protocols
* Protocol-specific filters
* RSSI and service UUID filters

Supported protocol configurations include:

* iBeacon
* AltBeacon
* Eddystone
* Generic BLE

See [`set_bleConfig`](set_bleConfig.md) for the complete request schema and configuration examples.

#### Step 3: Start BLE scanning

Use [`start`](start.md) and include `ble` in `payload.scanType`.

To start only BLE scanning, use:

```json
"scanType": [
  "ble"
]
```

To start BLE scanning and RFID inventory together, use:

```json
"scanType": [
  "ble",
  "rfid"
]
```

See [`start`](start.md) for the complete MQTT command examples.

> **Note:** Starting BLE scanning through `scanType` requires reader build `4.0.11` or later.

After BLE scanning starts, the reader publishes detected BLE devices and beacon advertisements through the configured data-event connection.

### Supported BLE beacon formats

The `data.beaconType` field identifies the detected beacon format.

| `data.beaconType` | Protocol-specific object | Description                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GENERIC_BLE`     | None                     | Reports the common BLE device and advertisement fields.                |
| `IBEACON`         | `data.iBeacon`           | Reports iBeacon fields such as UUID, major, minor, and transmit power. |
| `ALTBEACON`       | `data.altBeacon`         | Reports AltBeacon identification and signal-reference fields.          |
| `EDDYSTONE_URL`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone URL frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_UID`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone UID frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_EID`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone EID frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_TLM`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone telemetry frame.                                  |

A protocol-specific object is included only when it applies to the detected beacon format.

### Published BLE data event

A BLE Data Event contains:

* `type`, with the value `BLE_DATA`
* `timestamp`, indicating when the reader generated the event
* `eventNum`, containing the BLE event sequence number
* `data`, containing the detected device or beacon information

In a BLE Data Event, `eventNum` is a top-level field. In an RFID Tag Data Event, the sequence number is reported as `data.eventNum`.

#### BLE data event body

Use the **Sample BLE Data Event** tab to view examples for the supported beacon formats. Use the **BLE Data Event Schema** tab to review the complete event structure and field definitions.

type.description: BLE data event type.

timestamp.description: Event timestamp with UTC offset.

eventNum.description: BLE sequence number; published at envelope level.

data.description: BLE device or beacon information.

beaconType.description: Beacon format reported by the scanner.

iBeacon.description: iBeacon details when beaconType is IBEACON.

altBeacon.description: AltBeacon details when beaconType is ALTBEACON.

eddystone.description: Eddystone details. Fields depend on the frame type; the URL example illustrates one format.

url.description: Advertised URL for a URL frame.

After BLE scanning starts, the reader publishes detected BLE devices and beacon advertisements through the configured data-event connection.

### Supported BLE beacon formats

The `data.beaconType` field identifies the detected beacon format.

| `data.beaconType` | Protocol-specific object | Description                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GENERIC_BLE`     | None                     | Reports the common BLE device and advertisement fields.                |
| `IBEACON`         | `data.iBeacon`           | Reports iBeacon fields such as UUID, major, minor, and transmit power. |
| `ALTBEACON`       | `data.altBeacon`         | Reports AltBeacon identification and signal-reference fields.          |
| `EDDYSTONE_URL`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone URL frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_UID`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone UID frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_EID`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone EID frame.                                        |
| `EDDYSTONE_TLM`   | `data.eddystone`         | Reports an Eddystone telemetry frame.                                  |

A protocol-specific object is included only when it applies to the detected beacon format.

### Published BLE data event

A BLE Data Event contains:

* `type`, with the value `BLE_DATA`
* `timestamp`, indicating when the reader generated the event
* `eventNum`, containing the BLE event sequence number
* `data`, containing the detected device or beacon information

In a BLE Data Event, `eventNum` is a top-level field. In an RFID Tag Data Event, the sequence number is reported as `data.eventNum`.

#### BLE data event body

Use the **Sample BLE Data Event** tab to view examples for the supported beacon formats. Use the **BLE Data Event Schema** tab to review the complete event structure and field definitions.

| `STATUS` | `status` | Reports whether the user application is `running` or `stopped`. |
| `CPU` | `cpu` | Reports user-application CPU utilization as a percentage from 0 to 100. |
| `RAM` | `ram` | Reports user-application RAM utilization as a percentage from 0 to 100. |
| `UPTIME` | `uptime` | Reports how long the user application has been running. |
| `NUM_DATA_MESSAGES_RXED` | `numDataMessagesRxed` | Reports the number of data messages received by the application. |
| `NUM_DATA_MESSAGES_TXED` | `numDataMessagesTxed` | Reports the number of data messages sent by the application to Reader Gateway. |
| `INCOMING_DATA_BUFFER_PERCENTAGE_REMAINING` | `incomingDataBufferPercentageRemaining` | Reports the percentage of incoming buffer capacity remaining. |
| `OUTGOING_DATA_BUFFER_PERCENTAGE_REMAINING` | `outgoingDataBufferPercentageRemaining` | Reports the percentage of outgoing buffer capacity remaining. |

Each object in `data.userapps` also includes the application `name`.

#### Step 2: Apply the configuration

Apply the configuration using [`set_config`](set_config.md) for MQTT or `PUT /cloud/config` for REST. Select the corresponding example below to view the complete request.

### Published `userapps` data

The reader publishes the selected fields for each installed application in `data.userapps` as part of the complete heartbeat event.

#### Example heartbeat

Use the **Example** tab to view a heartbeat containing `userapps` data. Use the **Schema** tab to review the published field definitions.

post.description:
## Heartbeat Interval

The heartbeat interval determines how often the reader publishes a `heartbeat` event.

Configure the interval under:

```text
READER-GATEWAY.managementEventConfig.heartbeat.interval
```

The interval is specified in seconds:

* The default value is `60`.
* Set the value to `0` to disable heartbeat publication.

### Configure the heartbeat interval

Complete the following three steps in order.

#### Step 1: Set the interval

Choose the interval in seconds under `READER-GATEWAY.managementEventConfig.heartbeat.interval`. Use `0` to disable heartbeat publication.

#### Step 2: Apply the configuration

Send [`set_config`](set_config.md) for MQTT or `PUT /cloud/config` for REST. The following examples configure the reader to publish a heartbeat every 60 seconds.

#### Step 3: Verify heartbeat publication

After the configuration is applied, the reader publishes heartbeat events at the specified interval.

To configure the information included in each event or view the published event format, see [Heartbeat](heartbeat.md).

## Notification Events

Notification events report reader status changes on the management event channel. These events use `notification` as the value of the common management-event envelope `type` field.

The notification envelope is extensible so that different notification data objects can be documented without changing the common envelope.

> **Note:** The current release defines display-peripheral connection notifications on FXR readers with a display. Certificate-status and user-application installation notifications are not defined by the current Notification Event Schema and are not documented as supported event payloads.

### Display events

A Display Event is published when the connection status of a supported display peripheral changes.

Supported peripherals include:

* Monitor
* Keyboard
* Mouse
* Touch panel

A single event can report changes for one or more peripherals.

### Configure display event publishing

Complete the following three steps in order.

#### Step 1: Configure the management-event destination

Configure the management-event destination as described in [Configure Management Event Publishing](#tag-management-events-configure-management-event-publishing).

#### Step 2: Review automatic publication

> **Note:** Display Events do not have an enable or disable setting under `managementEventConfig`. The reader publishes them automatically when the connection status of a supported display peripheral changes.

#### Step 3: Check current peripheral status

Use [Get Input/Output Devices](get_inputOutputDevices.md) to retrieve the current status of the connected peripherals.

### Published display event

A Display Event uses the common management-event envelope with `type` set to `notification`. For definitions of the common envelope fields, see [Management Event Format](#tag-management-events-management-event-format).

Use the **Sample Display Event** tab to view events published by the reader. Use the **Display Event Schema** tab as the single reference for the complete payload, including the supported peripheral objects and their `status` values.

component.description: Event source: RG for Reader Gateway, RC for Radio Control, or the user application name.

GPIOLEDConfig.v1.title: GPIO-LED configuration
GPIOLEDConfig.v1.description:
GPIO-LED module configuration

Configure GPO and LED behaviour based on Events generated

Supported Events:
1. GPI_1_L: event raised when GPI 1 changed from HIGH to LOW
2. GPI_1_H: event raised when GPI 1 changed from LOW to HIGH
3. GPI_2_L: event raised when GPI 2 changed from HIGH to LOW
4. GPI_2_H: event raised when GPI 2 changed from LOW to HIGH
5. CLOUD_DISCONNECT: event raised when reader is disconnected from cloud
6. CLOUD_CONNECT: event raised when reader is connected to cloud
7. TAG_READ: event raised when a tag is read
8. RADIO_START: event raised when inventory operation started using START API
9. RADIO_STOP: event raised when inventory operation stopped using STOP API

delayBetweenAntennaCycles.v1.description:
This introduces a delay between antenna cycles if no tags are read or if no unique tags are read. This allows the reader to share the spectrum if there are no tags to be read. 

If absent, 
on the ATR7000 and the FX9600, delayBetweenAntennas cycles is set to wait for 75 mS if no unique tags are read during a antenna cycle.  
on the FX7500, delayBetweenAntennas cycles is set to wait for 75 mS if no tags are read during a antenna cycle.

operatingMode.v1.title: operatingMode
operatingMode.v1.description:
Represents the reader operating mode.

Cross-field constraints:
- accesses is not allowed in INVENTORY mode.
- query and filter with prefix cannot be configured at the same time.
- radioStartConditions and radioStopConditions are not allowed in PORTAL mode.
- reportFilter and accesses cannot both be set.
- accesses cannot be set with tagMetaData containing RESERVED, EPC, TID, or USER.
- reportFilter cannot be set with tagMetaData containing RESERVED, EPC, TID, or USER unless reportFilter.addl_keys is configured.
- transmitPower array length, antennaStopCondition array length, and query array length must match the size of antennas.

type.description: The type of mode of operation

modeSpecificSettings.description: One of inventorySettings or portalSettings, depending on the selected mode type.

environment.description:
The type of environment in which the reader operates. Along with the regulatory configuration of the reader, the environment parameter will set the default link profile parameters (i.e., Miller mode, BLF, Tari, etc.) and the receiver dynamic range (interference immunity).

  LOW_INTERFERENCE:  The reader is operating in an environment when the likelihood of interference is very low or only occurs for very brief periods of time (defined as a single interrogator environment in the Gen2 and ISO standards).

  HIGH_INTERFERENCE: The reader is operating in the presence of other readers (defined as a multi-interrogator or dense interrogator environment in the Gen2 and ISO standards).

  VERY_HIGH_INTERFERENCE: The reader is operating in an environment where the number of readers is greater than the number of available channels, or when interfering readers are in very close proximity to each other.

  AUTO_DETECT: This will cause the reader to try and assess the environment and adjust accordingly. 

  DEMO: Should be used when demonstrating the maximum performance (fastest read rate) of a reader. This assumes no other readers in the environment.

  If absent, the environment is set to HIGH_INTERFERENCE

antennas.description:
An array of integers representing the antenna ports to use to read tags.

 If absent, all antenna ports are used.

oneOf.description: Single value applies to all antennas

Each value applies to each antenna in the antennas array
Array length must match antennas array length

transmitPower.description:
Desired Transmit Power (in dbm).

 If absent, the value is set to 27 dbm.

 Cross-field constraint: when provided as an array, the array length must match the size of antennas.

oneOf.description:
Each value applies to each antenna in the antennas array
Array length must match antennas array length

antennaStopCondition.description:
Stop Condition for antennas. 

 If absent, the antenna stop condition is set to run a single inventory round for no longer than 1/N seconds. Where N is the number of enabled antennas.

oneOf.description:
Each value applies to each antenna in the antennas array
Array length must match antennas array length

query.description:
Gen2 query parameters. See Gen2 spec for details.

 If absent, "sel" is set to ALL, session is set to 1, target is set to A, and tag population set to 1.

 Cross-field constraints: cannot be configured at the same time as filter with prefix; when provided as an array, the array length must match the size of antennas.

selects.description:
Gen2 select parameters. See Gen2 spec for details.

 If absent, no select will be issued. Cannot be set when filter with prefix type is also set. 

 If there is an array of select objects, all of the selects in the array will be applied to all antennas.
 
 If there is an array of array of select objects, each array of select objects will apply to each antenna. The array of arrays must have the same number of entries as the antennas array.

delayAfterSelects.description: Duration in milliseconds to wait after issuing the final select before issuing a query. If absent, the minimum time will be used.

accesses.description:
Gen2 access parameters. See Gen2 spec for details.

 If absent, no access will be issued. 

 Cross-field constraints:
 - Cannot be set in INVENTORY mode.
 - Cannot be set at the same time as reportFilter.
 - Cannot be set at the same time as tagMetaData containing RESERVED/EPC/TID/USER.

 If there is an array of access objects, all of the accesss in the array will be applied to all antennas.
 
 If there is an array of array of access objects, each array of access objects will apply to each antenna. The array of arrays must have the same number of entries as the antennas array.

radioStartConditions.description:
Controls when, after a start command is issued, the radio starts trying to inventory tags.
This is distinct from antennaStopCondition.
Cross-field constraint: cannot be set in PORTAL mode.

radioStopConditions.description:
Controls when an ongoing radio operation completes.
This is distinct from antennaStopCondition.
Cross-field constraint: cannot be set in PORTAL mode.

reportFilter.description:
Controls when and how often a tag is reported.

Cross-field constraints:
- Cannot be set while in INVENTORY mode.
- Cannot be set at the same time as accesses.
- Cannot be set at the same time as tagMetaData containing RESERVED/EPC/TID/USER unless addl_keys is configured.

startTrigger.description: The GPI trigger to start reads on the portal

port.description: The GPI port to signal. If absent, port 1 is used.

signal.description: The signal value for the trigger. If absent, signal LOW is used

stopInterval.description: The interval at which to stop reads after the last unique tag is read (seconds). If absent, the reader will stop after not reading a unique tag in 3 seconds

radioStartConditions.v1.title: radioStartConditions
radioStartConditions.v1.description:
Controls when, after a “start” is issued, the radio starts trying to inventory tags. 

If absent, the radio will immediately begin inventorying tags upon a "start" command.

gpis.description: List of GPI pins used to trigger radio start

radioStopConditions.v1.title: radioStopConditions
radioStopConditions.v1.description:
Controls when an ongoing operation completes. 

If absent, the radio will continue trying to inventory tags until a "stop" is issued.

duration.description: Time to run until radio stops (in seconds)

antennaCycles.description: The number of cycles through all enabled antennas before stopping the radio

tagCount.description: The number of tags to inventory until the radio stops. Cannot be set at the same time as durationAfterNoMoreUniqueTags

durationAfterNoMoreUniqueTags.description: Duration (in seconds) after not inventorying any more unique tags to stop the radio. Cannot be set at the same time as tagCount

rssiFilter.v1.title: rssiFilter
rssiFilter.v1.description:
Tag with RSSI below threshold will not be inventoried by the radio

If absent, rssi filter is not used.

Note: Currently ONLY supported by the FX9600.

threshold.description: Threshold (in dbm) below which the radio will ignore a tag response

mask.description: Mask Field (see EPC Gen2 Spec). The value must be a hex string (only values 0-9 and a-f) and must have an even number of characters.

truncate.description: Truncate Field (see EPC Gen2 Spec) If absent, truncation is disabled. If non-zero, the value indicates the number of bits to expect in the tag response.

tagMetaData.v1.title: tagMetaData
tagMetaData.v1.description:
Controls the metadata that is sent when a tag is reported

  “ANTENNA” will report the antenna port upon which the tag was inventoried.

  “RSSI” will report the rssi (in dbm) of the inventoried tag. If the tag is only reported occasionally (see reportFilter), this tag will be the peak rssi since the last reported read.

   “PHASE” will report the phase (in degrees) of the inventoried tag. This value will only be reported if each individual tag read is reported (in other words, if reportFilter duration is set to 0). Otherwise, it will not be reported.

  “CHANNEL” will report the channel (in MHz) the reader was using when the tag was inventoried. This value will only be reported if each individual tag read is reported (in other words, if reportFilter duration is set to 0). Otherwise, it will not be reported.

  “SEEN_COUNT” will report the number of times the tag has been inventoried since the previous report. This value will always be 1 if each individual tag read is reported (in other words, if reportFilter duration is set to 0). 

  “PC” will report the PC bits of the inventoried tag as a hex string. 

  “XPC” will report the XPC bits of the inventoried tag, if present, as a hex string. 

  “CRC” will report the CRC bits of the inventoried tag as a hex string.

  “EPC” will report the entire contents of the EPC bank as a hex string. If only a portion of the memory bank is desired, this can be requested by appending a [] to the string and placing the words requested. For instance, if only the first word is desired, the value can be set as “EPC[1]”. If the first word and the 3-5 word are desired, the value can be set to “EPC[1,3-5]”.

  “TID” will report the entire contents of the TID bank as a hex string. If only a portion of the memory bank is desired, this can be requested by appending a [] to the string and placing the words requested. For instance, if only the first word is desired, the value can be set as “TID[1]”. If the first word and the 3-5 word are desired, the value can be set to “TID[1,3-5]”.

  “USER” will report the entire contents of the USER bank as a hex string. If only a portion of the memory bank is desired, this can be requested by appending a [] to the string and placing the words requested. For instance, if only the first word is desired, the value can be set as “TID[1]”. If the first word and the 3-5 word are desired, the value can be set to “TID[1,3-5]”.

  “MAC” will report the MAC Address of the reader reporting the tag.

  “HOSTNAME” will report the hostname of the reader reporting the tag.

  “READERLOCATION” will report the reader's configured location with the tag.

The array may also contain an object or objects. The object must contain a single name value pair with the name being set to “userDefined”, “antennaNames”, or “gpsCoordinates”.


If absent,
“SIMPLE” mode does not report any additional meta data, “PORTAL” and “CONVEYOR” modes reports “ANTENNA”, and “INVENTORY” mode reports “ANTENNA”, “RSSI”, and “SEEN_COUNT”.

userDefined.description: A user defined field to report each time a tag is reported

antennaNames.description:
Used to give antenna ports descriptive names
Length of array must match the number of antenna ports on the device

gpsCoordinates.description: GPS coordinates metadata reported with each tag event when location metadata is enabled.

tagReportFilter.v1.title: reportFilter
tagReportFilter.v1.description:
Controls when and how often a tag is reported

NOTE: This cannot be set while in "INVENTORY" mode. Setting the modeSpecificSetting for interval must be used in "INVENTORY" mode.

If absent, each mode uses a different default.

"SIMPLE": report tag read once.

"PORTAL" and "CONVEYOR": report each tag the first time it is read on each antenna.

duration.description:
Duration (in seconds) to wait to report a tag again once it has already been reported
It should be noted that the way the filter works is that as long as the tag is being read by the reader, it will not report unless the time since the previous report of this tag on this antenna meets the type and duration. 
Duration is a uint32 value and the max value is bound by the data type.

type.description: Configures the timeout (in seconds) by antenna or for entire radio

addl_keys.description:
Filters tag reports based on additional configured keys.

Supported value: TID.

Cross-field constraints:
- addl_keys can only contain TID when tagMetaData also contains TID, PC and CRC.
- When type is PER_ANTENNA and addl_keys contains TID, tagMetaData must also include ANTENNA.

tagidfilter.v1.title: tagIdFilter
tagidfilter.v1.description:
Represents filter on the tag id.

If absent, no filter is used.

Cross-field constraint: When match is set to prefix, query cannot be configured at the same time.

value.description:
The value to match.


For prefix and suffix filters. Only hex digits are allowed and there must be an even number of hex digits.

When prefix filter is used, selects cannot be used. 

For regex filter, C++ STL regex values should be used.
